newsitem.title: UK: UK's Major - involvement in EMU talks vital.
newsitem.headline: UK's Major - involvement in EMU talks vital.

text.p: Britain's Prime Minister John Major said on Tuesday it was vital to be involved in negotiations over a single European currency whether Britain joined or not.
He said the pound could soar, threatening Britain's trade position, if a weak single currency went ahead.
"We have a real stake in what happens here," he said on BBC radio.
"If we are there in the negotiations, whether we join a single currency or not we may be able to stop other people doing something silly with a single currency," Major said.

"If it went ahead in the wrong economic circumstances and you had a weak single currency, money from around the world...would go into the two hard currencies of Europe, the Swiss Franc and sterling," he said.
The exchange rate of sterling would soar and Britain's competitiveness would be threatened as a result.
The government officially retains a wait-and-see policy on European economic and monetary union, which is scheduled to go ahead on January 1, 1999.
Over the weekend, Health Secretary Stephen Dorrell said Britain would not join a European single currency in 1999, sparking a row in the ruling party weeks before the election.
Major told BBC radio he had made a mistake.
